title: Comments
summary: Comments are notes for humans inside code. The computer ignores them completely. Good comments explain WHY code does something, not what it
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Comments are notes for humans inside code. The computer ignores them completely. Good comments explain WHY code does something, not what it does — the code already says what.
Every language has its own comment style. Some use a symbol at the start of a line, others use block markers. Knowing yours saves you from accidentally breaking programs.
Key points: comments never affect output, use them for tricky logic, and remove stale comments when code changes.

sections.codeExample:
; This program greets the world
section .data
    msg db "Hello, World!", 10
section .text
    global _start
_start:
    mov eax, 4
    mov ebx, 1
    mov ecx, msg
    mov edx, 14
    int 0x80
    mov eax, 1
    xor ebx, ebx
    int 0x80
